column3: The Hebrew calls these the sons of Judah; BSB uses descendants.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has the singular father of Etam where BSB has sons of Etam. It explicitly says the name of their sister rather than using a passive naming clause.
The Hebrew calls these the sons of Hur; BSB uses descendants.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls these the sons of Naarah; BSB uses descendants.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew begins a new clause, and Koz fathered; BSB places Koz after the preceding list with and Koz, who was the father.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew reinforces the blessing by repeating the verb and ends with what he asked; BSB uses bless without that repetition and explicitly names Jabez again.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew lists Hathath alone as Othniel’s offspring here; BSB also includes Meonothai in this verse.
The Hebrew calls Joab the father of the valley of craftsmen and says they were craftsmen; BSB supplies its inhabitants and explicitly explains how the place received its name.
The Hebrew has sons of Elah in the plural before naming Kenaz; BSB uses son in the singular.
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew introduces Ezrah’s offspring with singular son and leaves the conceiving woman unnamed; BSB uses sons and identifies the mother as Mered’s wife Bithiah, describing birth rather than conception.

The Hebrew first describes his Judean wife bearing children and then identifies Bithiah’s sons and her marriage to Mered; BSB moves the Bithiah statement first and describes Mered taking the Judean wife.
The Hebrew uses the singular father before Keilah; BSB supplies the plural fathers.
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew says the words or matters are ancient; BSB describes these names as coming from ancient records.

The Hebrew calls these the sons of Simeon; BSB uses descendants.
The Hebrew gives a successive chain, Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son; BSB presents all three as sons of Shaul.
The Hebrew gives Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son; BSB presents all three as sons of Mishma.
The Hebrew says his brothers did not have many sons; BSB uses children.
